exposure: household wealth (rich and very rich households)
cohort: The study included mothers and their newborn babies in Guinea, identified from the 2018 Demographic and Health Survey (DHS).
finding: Less than half (42.8%) of women in Guinea initiated breastfeeding within the first hour of life, with caesarean delivery, unassisted delivery, unemployment, small birth size, and belonging to poorer households being negatively associated with early initiation.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was negatively associated with early initiation of breastfeeding (aOR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.16-0.53, p < 0.001).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from the 2018 Demographic and Health Survey (DHS), focusing on breastfeeding initiation within the first hour of life.
birth_weight: Small birth size (categorically mentioned, no specific weight range)
